profiling.cloneChanges: Only import/createCpuProfiler; mark on existing phase entry; finish in finally. All existing load/parse/expand/check/emit/export/import/smoke operations retained.

metricScopes.processCpu: process.cpuUsage is the entire Node process, including helper/concurrent V8 threads; not worker-isolate-only CPU.
metricScopes.workerCpu: Inspector CPU profiles sample the local worker isolate. Each phase has its own denominator. GC samples measure this isolate profiling category, not total/concurrent GC CPU.
metricScopes.allocation: Heap sampling byte weights estimate cumulative worker-isolate allocation, including collected objects. Not exact bytes, not exact allocation counts, and not live/RSS/retained memory.
metricScopes.cgroup: cpu.stat/memory.peak cover the guarded cgroup tree; distinct from process and isolate metrics.
metricScopes.hardware: perf probe reports cycles/instructions <not supported>; no compiler hardware-cycle/instruction measurements.

observerLimitations: CPU Profiler.start precedes HeapProfiler.startSampling in unchanged helper; inspector post/startSampling overhead enters CPU sample profiles before helper wall/processCPU timers begin. E.g. write-and-hash sample span636.741ms vs helper wall221.944ms; small phase samples are observer dominated. No subtraction-based performance claim.
Helper stops CPU before allocation sampler; profile materialization can allocate while heap sampling remains active. Raw profiles retain observer/inspector sites.
Phase intervals run mark-to-next-mark/finish and include interphase validation. Overall times include profile serialization; all timings instrumented, not comparable as normal benchmarks.
Heap tree selfSize sum and sampling-record size sum differ slightly; both retained as statistical estimates rather than asserting exact allocation accounting.
CPU sampling self attribution can fold inlined work into callers; allocation sites and real call stacks are complementary evidence, not proof of isolated causal cost.

allocationFindings.statement: Map-family sites account for about22.1% of sampled check allocation estimates. Top Map.hi11.19GB,Map.lo9.30GB,Map.get.go8.30GB. Heap stacks connect these through checker_arena.name to checker_body_arena_names_cons. Source6942-6946 constructs Tuple+MNode during map rebuilding; no exact object count inferred.
Heap stacks connect to checker_body_whnf and checker_body_core_subst_open. Source11366 constructs Tuple+Arena after Array.get; observed aggregate-record allocation, not just a generic helper label.

Source31951-31964 constructs CheckerPending/CheckerDirect/Finished wrappers and closures for substitution paths. Heap data measures allocation sites; it does not attribute all logical substitution CPU.

Top index_lookup.find.go1.42GB via emitter_body_js_constructor_lookup; emitter_body_js_quote_chars1.41GB and emitter_continuation_27 1.00GB via emitted per-character CPS path. Check and emit have separate sample denominators.
